newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end lower as properties slump.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end lower as properties slump.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were dragged to a sharply lower close on Wednesday as investors sold down property counters on concerns about the outlook for the territory's property market, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index tumbled 133.07 points, or 1.00 percent, to 13,119.13. Turnover was HK$11.90 billion compared with HK$13.37 billion on Tuesday.
"The big (property) developers are all under pressure. I think there is a definite sign that property prices cannot continue to spiral," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.

But he said there were also concerns that if prices did continue to spike higher, the government could intervene to stamp out speculation. "The market wants to take everything negatively at the moment," Osborn said.

Police bomb disposal experts exploded a suspicious parcel on Wednesday morning which was apparently planted outside Hong Kong's legislature by a resident furious about spiralling property prices in the territory.
Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd dropped HK$1.75 to HK$71.75 and New World Development Co Ltd slid HK$1.80 to HK$43.10.
"This nervousness in the market is linked to concerns on the general interest rate scenario," said Miles Remington, sales trader at SocGen-Crosby Securities.
He said investors were turning their attention to second line stocks and red chips.
Shenzhen Expressway Co Ltd made its market debut on Wednesday and closed at HK$2.775 compared to an initial public offering price of HK$2.20 per share.
The stock soared to a high of HK$3.375 during the morning session and strong early demand for the shares caused a back-up in trade executions, the Hong Kong stock exchange said.
Shenzhen Expressway was the most active stock of the session with volume of 341 million shares.
"Most of the turnover is occurring in the China shares and red chips. The rest of the market is pretty quiet," said Osborn.
Hysan Development Co Ltd posted a 10 percent rise in 1996 net profit on Wednesday to HK$1.35 billion.
Analysts had expected net profit growth of about 13 percent and the stock closed HK$0.75 lower at HK$24.50.
Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd was due to release 1996 results after the close. The stock rose HK$0.05 to HK$12.00.
